newsitem.title: INDIA: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 10.
newsitem.headline: INDIAN HEADLINE STOCKS - factors to watch - March 10.

text.p: Following are some of the main factors affecting Indian stock markets on Monday morning:
NEWS OUTLOOK:

** Indian stock markets will tread carefully this week as the fizz settles after a 16 percent surge in values prompted by last month's federal budget which slashed taxes and boosted industry morale, brokers say
** India's main communist party, a key member of the ruling coalition, says it will fight some market-opening steps outlined in the federal budget
Harkishen Singh Surjeet, general secretary of the
Communist Party of India-Marxist (CPI-M), says his party will seek to reverse tax and import tariff cuts and a partial opening of the insurance market announced in the budget
** International credit rating agency Moody's puts India on credit watch, indicating a negative outlook, a week after the federal budget, the weekend Business Line newspaper says
The current assessment is part of a regular six-monthly
review, the newspaper says

** India's says foreign institutional investors can invest in all dated government securities except treasury bills. The securities can be bought at auctions or floatations and from the secondary market, the Reserve Bank of India says.
Secondary market trades will be through stock markets or
over-the-counter with SGL account holders and will be governed by the RBI's delivery versus payment settlement system
** Year-on-year inflation rate measured by the wholesale price index fell to 7.91 percent in the week ending February 22 from 7.99 percent in the previous week
** Foreign exchange reserves surged to $20.08 billion in the week ended March 6, the Business Standard reports

** Former finance minister Manmohan Singh tells the Economic Times that the budget has squandered resources on open-ended subsidies, cut too many taxes too fast, and failed to step up public investment in the rural sector or address the question of a burgeoning oil pool account
MARKETS:

** The 30-share index of the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) .BSESN closed 64.95 points, or 1.65 percent, lower at 3876.04 on Thursday in end-account trade. Stock markets across the country were closed for a religious holiday on Friday
STOCKS TO WATCH:
** Shares of India's state-run overseas telecommunications monopoly, Videsh Sanchar Nigam Ltd seen in the limelight as it begins roadshows for a long-awaited issue of global depositary receipts
The issue is worth $567 million at the current market
price. VSNL shares ended 38 rupees up at 1,075 on Thursday

** Larsen & Toubro has identified Sri Lanka and Bangladesh as potential markets for cement, the Financial Express says. The firm plans to set up clinker grinding units in these countries with capacities of 500,000-700,000 tonnes
